question: What is the primary anatomical purpose of creating a colostomy?

options.A: Increasing water absorption in the small intestine
options.B: Rerouting fecal matter through the abdominal wall
options.C: Restoring normal sphincter control after rectal surgery
options.D: Permanently curing chronic inflammatory bowel disease

explanation: A colostomy creates a surgical opening to divert stool away from a diseased or injured lower bowel segment. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h1)

question: A patient with a gunshot wound to the abdomen most likely needs a colostomy for which reason?

options.A: Palliative care for advanced colon cancer

explanation: Trauma injuries like gunshot wounds often cause bowel perforation, requiring rapid surgical diversion to prevent peritonitis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which type of colostomy produces liquid and highly irritating stool?
explanation: An ascending colostomy is located high in the bowel tract, resulting in liquid output containing active digestive enzymes that easily irritate skin. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h2)

question: Why is the output of a sigmoid colostomy typically solid and formed?

options.A: Bile salts are completely absent from the digestive tract
options.B: Dietary fiber intake is strictly restricted postoperatively
options.C: The surgical procedure removes the entire large intestine
options.D: Most water absorption has already occurred in the colon

explanation: As waste travels through the entire length of the colon before reaching the sigmoid section, maximum water reabsorption takes place, solidifying the stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h2)

question: What is the expected appearance of a healthy, viable intestinal stoma?

options.A: Dark purple with a smooth surface
options.B: Pale, dry, and cool to touch
options.D: White and completely flat with skin

explanation: A healthy stoma has a rich blood supply, making it appear pink or red and moist, similar to the mucous membrane inside the mouth. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h3)

question: A newly formed stoma appears dark purple and dry during the morning shift assessment. What action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Document the finding as normal postoperative swelling
options.B: Notify the surgeon immediately regarding compromised blood supply
options.C: Irrigate the stoma gently with sterile normal saline
options.D: Apply a hydrocolloid powder to absorb excess moisture

explanation: A dark purple, dusky, or black stoma indicates ischemia or necrosis, which is a surgical emergency requiring immediate provider notification. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h3)

question: How much skin should remain exposed between the stoma and the cut edge of the barrier?
explanation: A small gap of one to two millimeters prevents the adhesive barrier from cutting into the stoma while protecting the surrounding skin from corrosive effluent. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why is it important to gently push down on the newly applied skin barrier for about thirty seconds?

options.A: It forces trapped air bubbles out of the stomal lumen
options.B: Body heat activates the pressure-sensitive adhesive for a secure seal
options.C: Continuous pressure stops minor postoperative stomal bleeding
options.D: It flattens out normal postoperative abdominal wall creases

explanation: Gentle pressure and body warmth help the adhesive backing conform tightly to skin contours, preventing leaks. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h4)

question: Which food item places a patient with a colostomy at the highest risk for a mechanical bowel blockage?
explanation: High-fiber, poorly digestible items like popcorn, nuts, and corn kernels easily lodge in the stoma opening, causing a blockage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h5)

question: What dietary advice should a nurse give a patient troubled by excessive stoma gas?

options.A: Avoid carbonated drinks and chewing gum
options.B: Eliminate all dairy products from the diet
options.D: Increase intake of raw cabbage and beans

explanation: Swallowing air through gum chewing or consuming carbonated beverages directly increases gas production in the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h5)

question: What term describes the abnormal sinking of the stoma below the level of the abdominal wall?
explanation: Retraction occurs when the stoma pulls inward below skin level, making pouching difficult and causing severe leakage issues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h6)

question: Which clinical finding is most indicative of a parastomal hernia?

options.A: A visible bulge around the stoma site when straining
options.B: Continuous bright red bleeding from the stoma tip
options.C: Complete absence of fecal output for forty-eight hours
options.D: Sudden black discoloration of the mucosal tissue

explanation: A parastomal hernia is a type of incisional hernia where abdominal contents push through the weakened muscle layer surrounding the stoma, creating a noticeable bulge. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h6)

question: What is the best initial approach when teaching a newly admitted patient how to care for their colostomy?

options.A: Ask family members to take over all care permanently
options.B: Wait until discharge day to demonstrate the pouch change
options.C: Encourage them to look at and touch the stoma gradually
options.D: Provide a complex manual to read independently overnight

explanation: Gradual exposure helps patients overcome anxiety and body image distress, fostering self-reliance at a comfortable pace. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h7)

question: Which resource is most valuable for helping a patient adjust emotionally to life with a permanent colostomy?

options.A: Stoma support groups and peer visitors
options.C: Advanced surgical textbooks on bowel resection

explanation: Interacting with individuals successfully living with a colostomy provides powerful reassurance and practical coping strategies. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h7)
